target_customer: Healthcare clinics, especially mid-sized and large ones
problem: Clinics juggle capacity planning, scheduling, credentialing and payroll across disconnected tools. Planbase combines them into an AI-native workforce platform.
business_model: B2B SaaS for clinics (pricing not public)

founders.name: Jack Light
founders.background_notes: Press describes the two founders as a married couple.

founders.name: Joe Shearman
previous_startups: Elando.ai, scheduling and sales forecasting for over 1,000 businesses per YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: Forecasting, scheduling optimization and payroll integration are standard but broad engineering; the founders had prior forecasting experience.

defensibility.rationale: Payroll and credentialing integrations add stickiness, but established scheduling vendors cover similar functions.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established workforce vendors persisted; no source found of Planbase being copied or acquired.

market_need_then: Clinic staffing and admin burden is a recurring pain; the company claims clinics save hundreds of hours a month (press release claim).

branding.domain_note: joinplanbase.com (join prefix); other unrelated products named Planbase exist

brand_strength.rationale: Generic compound name that collides with unrelated Planbase products; trade press covered the launch but not the brand.

outcome_analysis: Planbase launched publicly in November 2025 with a 2.1 million dollar seed and is still active in 2026 coverage. Repeat founders with forecasting experience from Elando give it execution credibility. It targets a crowded workforce management market and has little public traction data yet.
notes: CB Insights lists Phoenix Court instead of LocalGlobe, secondary data. Customer figure of 5,000 providers appears in one outlet only. Competitor search returned undated 2026 comparison pages and nothing on Planbase, so the list is empty. Company website fetch showed little content.
